subject: Clarify security exhibit: evidence cadence, sampling thresholds & data residency carveouts
messages:
From: Alex Martin <security@helioshealth.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Helios Health Legal <legal@helioshealth.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify security exhibit: sampling thresholds & data residency carveouts

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the materials — we're working through the security exhibit and have a couple of specific asks so we can move the order form forward:

1) Evidence cadence: Can you confirm how often Redwood rotates SOC 2 evidence (snapshots, control artifacts)? We typically require either quarterly snapshots or an annual attestation plus monthly telemetry for critical controls.

2) Pen test scope and sampling: Our security team wants clear language for sampling thresholds (how many hosts/sessions can be included in a sample, whether Redwood will provide logs vs. direct access).

3) Data residency carveout: We need to understand whether inspection rights (on-prem/staging access for pen test and evidence review) can be scoped to exclude APAC tenant data due to Helios' regulatory requirements. If Redwood can propose alternative evidence workflows for APAC data, that would be helpful.

We attached our vendor questionnaire for reference (helios_vendor_questionnaire.pdf). Would appreciate a short note back today with the recommended language we can share with legal, or an ETA for a redline.

Thanks,
Alex Martin
Security Lead, Helios Health
security@helioshealth.com

[attachment: helios_vendor_questionnaire.pdf]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify security exhibit: sampling thresholds & data residency carveouts

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline and a proposed next step:

1) Evidence cadence: Redwood maintains an annual SOC 2 report (Type II) and can provide quarterly control snapshots for high-risk controls on request. For telemetry (e.g., auth logs, audit trails) we can provide rolling 30/90-day extracts; if Helios needs monthly snapshots we can include that in the order form as an add-on.

2) Pen test sampling: We typically propose limited-scope testing (staging environment) with two options: a) provide sanitized log extracts and scoped artifacts, or b) grant short-lived read-only access to a dedicated staging environment (ephemeral credentials, jumpbox, MFA). We recommend specifying an upper bound on sample size (e.g., up to 10 hosts or 5% of sessions) and an acceptance criteria clause so both sides agree before testing.

3) Data residency carveout: We can scope inspection rights to exclude identified APAC tenant data. In practice we'd define a list of tenant IDs/regions in the security exhibit and provide alternative evidence (e.g., attestation plus additional logs) for APAC. That approach preserves Helios' constraints while keeping the audit playbook intact.

I'm looping in Laura and Karthik from Legal to propose redline language and a short phased approach (initial doc redline, then a joint triage call). Attached a first-pass response doc for the questionnaire.

Proposed next step: Legal redline and a 30-minute bridge to finalize sampling thresholds on WED 2026-05-06 at 10:00 PT. Does that work?

Best,
Rachel Kim

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify security exhibit: sampling thresholds & data residency carveouts

Rachel/Karthik — adding legal context and suggested redlines. High level: we should aim for precise, narrow language that preserves Helios' comfort but protects Redwood from overly broad inspection demands. Key suggestions below; redline attached.

- Audit rights: Limit to "reasonable business hours" and require 14 days' notice for any on-site/staging access. Prefer "inspection-lite" language: sampled evidence delivery or access to a dedicated staging environment rather than production access.

- Sampling thresholds: Define sampling as "up to 10 hosts or up to 5% of production sessions in scope, whichever is smaller," and require a mutually agreed test plan 5 business days prior. Add explicit non-exhaustive list of data types excluded (PII stored in APAC systems) if necessary.

- Data residency carveouts: Acceptable to carve out APAC tenant data where law prohibits cross-border access; require Redwood to provide alternative evidence (attestation + log extracts) and, where feasible, local-attested SOC 2 equivalent.

- Evidence retention: Propose Redwood retain sampled evidence for 90 days post-exchange unless otherwise requested in writing.

- Escrow/escrow alternative: Offer an evidence escrow (encrypted snapshot in S3 with access controls) as an optional order-form add-on; not included by default.

I've attached a redline (security_exhibit_redline_v1.docx). Suggest Karthik finalize legal-specific wording and we send a combined reply to Helios with the redline and a DocuSign order form option.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Security
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
[attachment: security_exhibit_redline_v1.docx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarify security exhibit: sampling thresholds & data residency carveouts

Thanks Laura — I've captured the legal edits and made a couple commercial/ops clarifications in the attached PDF. Quick summary of additions from my side:

- Pen test environment: Require testing to occur in a non-production staging environment provisioned by Redwood (or in a mutually agreed customer-managed staging instance). Access will be time-boxed, read-only where possible, and require ephemeral credentials + MFA.

- Sample scope confirmation: Add a clause that both parties will sign a Test Plan (appendix) at least 5 business days before execution listing hosts, endpoints, and acceptance criteria.

- Evidence handback: Redwood will provide sanitized logs and artifact extracts; full forensic images are not required unless mutually agreed and subject to additional NDAs and SOW.

- Retention: We will retain exchanged sample artifacts for 90 days. If Helios needs extended retention, include as an add-on in the order form.

- DocuSign: Included a link in the email for the revised order form (see related links). If Helios is good with the redline, we can route the Order Form + Assurance Addendum via DocuSign and include the evidence escrow option as a selectable checkbox.

I'll set up the WED 10:00 PT call for triage. If Helios prefers earlier, let me know.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Legal Operations
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
